records.claim: On a pipeline squash, tracking table entries with valid == 0 matching squashed ROB indices are invalidated by clearing payload and decay_ctr to 0.
records.open_question: How does the register tracking table recover on a branch misprediction squash? Section 5 states that recovering the Tomasulo-like table is deferred to future work, so the paper does not specify whether pending squashed entries are simply cleared or prior architectural values/digests are restored.

records.claim: Instructions that completed execution before branch misprediction resolution preserve their valid digests in the tracking table upon restart.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: Establishes that instructions finishing before branch resolution retain valid digests that enlarge visible register state upon restart.

records.claim: The register tracking table contains 65 entries indexed directly by logical register ID.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register.
records.why: Confirms the tracking table is dedicated and has one entry per logical register.

records.claim: Each tracking table entry consists of a 1-bit valid flag, a 14-bit payload holding either a ROB index or a 12-bit digest, and an 8-bit decay counter initialized to 256.
records.quote: Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: Directly defines the entry bit fields for valid and payload.

records.claim: The register tracking table storage cost is 1,495 bits.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Specifies 23 bits per entry across 65 registers in Table 3, yielding 1,495 bits.

records.claim: The register tracking table is directly indexed by logical register ID.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register.
records.why: Confirms direct one-to-one mapping per logical register.

records.claim: The default number of logical registers is 65.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Confirms 8 banks of 8 or 9 registers, totalling 65 logical registers (Bank 0 has 9, Banks 1-7 have 8).

records.claim: The default decay interval is 256 decoded instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Explicitly defines the 256 instruction decode threshold for digest invalidation.

records.claim: An integer register 12-bit digest is generated by XOR-folding 6-bit trailing count, 6-bit leading count shifted left by 3, and 6-bit register LSBs shifted left by 6.
records.quote: (1) For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Specifies the three 6-bit fields combined to produce the integer digest.

records.claim: A condition-code register 12-bit digest is formed by replicating the 4-bit flag pattern three times.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Directly specifies the 3x replication of 4 flag bits into a 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Each bank selects the register with the highest summed usefulness weight among available registers to query WT0, WT1, and WT2.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Establishes that the most useful available register digest is chosen and forwarded to the weight tables.

records.claim: When a bank's usefulness is non-positive, multiplier selects x0 and the bank contributes 0 to sR.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Confirms the per-bank scaling multiplier selects x0 when not deemed useful.

records.claim: When a bank's usefulness is positive, multiplier scales the WT sum by 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Confirms the per-bank scaling multiplier scales by 2.5 when useful.

records.claim: A register digest is invalidated and marked unavailable after 256 instructions are decoded without a new write.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Directly settles digest invalidation after 256 decoded instructions.

records.claim: Instructions completing before branch misprediction resolution retain valid digests upon restart while squashed instructions are invalidated.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: Confirms that instructions completed prior to branch resolution expand valid register visibility upon restart.

records.claim: Training updates correlations for registers available at prediction time, randomly selecting one register per bank when multiple are available.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Settles that training randomly selects one available register per bank to satisfy the single write-port constraint.

records.claim: The function update_sr represents an undefined policy call in the spec.
records.quote: The basic structure of RUNLTS is the same as that of TAGE-SC, consisting of multiple tagged tables and an SC.
records.why: Refutes the warning: update_sr is the entry point defined by algorithm 4 itself, adhering to the SC update interface of baseline TAGE-SC.

records.claim: Register digests for training are re-read directly from register_tracking_table at commit time rather than snapshotted at prediction time.
records.open_question: Are register digests saved in branch pipeline metadata at prediction time or read directly from register_tracking_table at commit? Reading at commit risks reading overwritten or decayed values rather than the digest visible at prediction time.

records.claim: Usefulness weights in UT are updated by incrementing by 1 if the bank WT prediction direction matched the actual branch outcome, and decrementing by 1 otherwise.
records.open_question: What is the exact update rule and condition for usefulness table (UT) weights? Section 4.2 states that UT tracks prediction usefulness but does not define whether usefulness increments based on WT agreement with branch outcome, or only when the register component corrects a baseline misprediction.

records.claim: WT0..2 and UT0..2 tables are indexed using hash functions hash_wt0..2(pc, digest) and hash_ut0..2(pc).
records.open_question: What are the exact hash functions used to index WT0, WT1, WT2 and UT0, UT1, UT2? The paper states 'PC + reg. digest' is hashed into h0, h1, h2 and PC is skewed for UT, but provides no hash formulas.

records.claim: Correlations are trained only for registers that were valid and available at prediction time, selecting one at random per bank.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time. If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Directly validates the note on training eligibility and random single-register selection.

records.claim: wt_tables consists of 8 banks, each containing 3 direct-mapped tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries), totalling 7,168 entries.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Confirms the three weight table sizes per bank (512, 256, 128) across the 8 banks.

records.claim: Each WT entry is a 6-bit signed saturating counter weight [-32, 31].
records.why: Specifies 6-bit weight width across all WT entries in Table 3.

records.claim: Total storage capacity of wt_tables is 43,008 bits.
records.why: Confirms total WT storage equals 43,008 bits.

records.claim: WT tables are indexed by hashing branch PC and the selected 12-bit register digest into indices h0, h1, and h2.
records.quote: Selected digest plus PC form the input labelled "PC + reg. digest", hashed into "h0", "h1", "h2".
records.why: Confirms the hash inputs for WT0, WT1, and WT2 are branch PC and the selected register digest.

records.claim: ut_tables consists of 8 banks with 3 tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each, tracking 9 registers in Bank 0 and 8 in Banks 1-7.
records.quote: Each entry of the first table holds an eight- (or nine-) element vector of weights reflecting the usefulness of each register.
records.why: Specifies that each UT entry stores an 8- or 9-element weight vector corresponding to the registers in that bank.

records.claim: Each UT entry contains a vector of 6-bit signed saturating usefulness weights (9 in Bank 0, 8 in Banks 1-7).
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Confirms 9x6-bit weight vectors in Bank 0 and 8-entry UT0, UT1, and UT2.

records.claim: Total storage capacity of ut_tables is 9,360 bits.
records.quote: UT: 6 bits x 65 regs x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3) = 9360 bits
records.why: Confirms total UT storage equals 9,360 bits.

records.claim: UT tables are indexed by PC skewed with 3 distinct hash functions to produce 3-bit indices for UT0, UT1, and UT2.
records.quote: Input "PC (skewed)".
records.why: Confirms skewed PC indexing into the 8-entry UT tables.

records.claim: The default number of banks in the register component is 8.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Directly specifies 8 banks for the register component.

records.claim: The default capacity of WT0 is 512 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Directly states 512 entries for WT0.

records.claim: The default capacity of WT1 is 256 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Directly states 256 entries for WT1.

records.claim: The default capacity of WT2 is 128 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1", "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Directly states 128 entries for WT2.

records.claim: The default capacity of each usefulness table (UT0, UT1, UT2) is 8 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Directly states 8 entries for each usefulness table.

records.claim: The useful multiplier default value is 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Confirms the scaling multiplier factor when useful is 2.5.

records.claim: The default WT counter weight width is 6 bits.
records.why: Table 3 defines the WT weight bit width as 6 bits.

records.claim: The default UT usefulness weight width is 6 bits.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Specifies 6-bit width for each usefulness weight.
